business_scope.primary_industry_name: Remote Desktop Access and Unattended Machine Telemetry Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: U.S.-derived common law heritage, local statutory law, and Marshallese customary law; the Business Corporations Act 1990 is modeled in substantial part on the Delaware General Corporation Law. Judicial review is exercised by the RMI High Court and RMI Supreme Court.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: No standalone bilateral investment treaty or comprehensive double taxation agreement is currently in force for the Republic of the Marshall Islands.

United States–Republic of the Marshall Islands Amended Compact of Free Association (1986, as amended 2003) contains economic, trade, and investment-related commitments for U.S. persons, but is not a BIT or DTA.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act 1990, as amended (codified at Title 29 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code), together with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2014, as amended, the AML/CFT Regulations 2015, and the confidential UBO register requirements administered by the Registrar of Corporations and supervised by the Financial Services Regulatory Commission. The UBO register is not public; access is permitted only to the Registrar, FSRC, the Financial Intelligence Unit, and other competent authorities acting under lawful process.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, shareholders, UBOs, signatories, and commercial counterparties against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, U.S. OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, RMI domestic AML/CFT enforcement lists, and, where relevant, Stripe and Paddle excluded-party databases. PEPs, PEP family members, and PEP close associates are treated as higher-risk; enhanced due diligence must include source of wealth, source of funds, transaction purpose, and senior management approval. Adverse media and negative news searches are required before incorporation and annually thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Republic of the Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations - official corporate registry and online name reservation portal administered by the Office of the Registrar, Majuro
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory corporate names must be expressed in Latin script. Marshallese and English are the official languages, and names in either language using standard Roman/Latin characters are accepted. Any proposed non-Latin script name must be transliterated into Latin characters; the Latin transliteration is the controlling legal name. No separate statutory translation is required for remote desktop software activities, but the name must be clearly distinguishable from all reserved and registered business names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of name rejection, the applicant receives a formal refusal notice from the Registrar. The applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar within 14 days, attaching the rejection notice, the proposed corporate name, a statement of distinguishing features, and any required ministerial or regulatory consent. The Registrar must decide the appeal within 15 business days. If the appeal is refused, the applicant may seek judicial review before the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands. Name reservations may be extended for one additional 30-day period upon verified administrative processing delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as the statutory registered office of an RMI Business Corporation. The BC must maintain a physical registered office in the Republic of the Marshall Islands with a licensed registered agent. Operational staff and the remote desktop/IoT software business may be managed remotely from any location, but service of process, corporate records, and the registered office address must remain at a physical RMI location. A virtual mailing address or remote-work location may be used commercially only if it is not designated as the statutory registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 5% likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Registrar or FSRC during the first 12 months for a low-risk, non-regulated remote software company. The risk rises to approximately 15-20% if the UBO or payment transaction profile triggers PEP, sanctions, adverse-media, or AML/CFT risk escalation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, B.C.A., Republic of the Marshall Islands (Title 24 R.M.I. Code), as amended, particularly Sections 29 (Articles of Incorporation), 32 (Registered Office and Resident Agent), 42 (Directors), and 51 (Officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a non-resident Business Corporation; nominal or no-par-value share capital is permitted, and no escrow deposit or bank-account blocking requirement applies before incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Incorporators and the initial Subscribers adopt the actions taken at this First Meeting of the Board. RESOLVED, that the Corporation subscribes to its initial capital per the Articles of Incorporation. RESOLVED, that the registered office stated in the Articles, at the office of the Resident Agent, is adopted. RESOLVED, that the nominated Resident Agent, Directors and Officers are appointed. RESOLVED, that the Corporate Secretary is directed to file all instruments, pay the statutory fees, and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation. RESOLVED, that all steps taken by management to select and engage payment processors, including Stripe and Paddle, are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro, R.M.I.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-reservation application via the online R.M.I. corporate registry portal. The proposed entity name must include the required corporate suffix 'Business Corporation' or 'BC'. Upon approval, the name is reserved for 30 days, within which the Articles of Incorporation must be filed.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the applicant incorporator's passport or ID
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, the applicant may submit an amended name proposition or contest the registry determination through a written explanation to the Registrar within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, Execute, and Submit Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro, R.M.I.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Articles of Incorporation setting out the corporate name, registered office, Resident Agent's R.M.I. address, authorised shares, par value, initial Directors, and the purpose to conduct remote desktop and unattended machine telemetry software services. Execute the Articles before a notary or with an electronic acceptance, and file them together with the required consents and the statutory filing fee.
required_dossiers: Signed and notarized Articles of Incorporation
Details of issued shares and subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or deficiency notice, the incorporators must file a supplemental statement or amended resolution within 10 business days curing the listed items and resubmit the corrected set.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro, R.M.I.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After confirming the Articles are compliant and the fee is paid, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The Certificate is the conclusive proof of formation and is delivered electronically to the submitting attorney or authorised representative.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate is delayed or errors are made in the corporate data, the Representative may file a formal correction request with the Registry supporting a reissue without substantive re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors, internal corporate record.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first organizational meeting of the initial Directors, or execute a unanimous written consent, adopting the Bylaws, ratifying the issuance of shares, adopting the registered office and Resident Agent, and appointing the President, Secretary, and Treasurer. Record the minutes in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Notice or waiver of notice of organizational meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any appointment or ratification is later contested, the board may adopt an amending resolution and re-execute the relevant consents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Finance, Revenue and Customs; Majuro Municipal Authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a General Business Licence with the Municipal Authority of Majuro and obtain a Tax Identification Number with the Revenue and Customs Office. The business licence will allow the corporation to invoice customers and accept payment-rail integration contracts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal or revenue authority queries the application, the applicant must respond with clarifying entity details or amend the stated business activity description to match registered corporate objects.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the corporation is a non-manufacturing software-publishing and telecommunication service entity; no industrial licensing board is triggered.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required; general municipal Business Licence suffices for office-based remote-support and software operation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — remote desktop software and telemetry services are non-industrial, office-based activities; no EIA registration or full EIA Report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOCs, or hazardous waste streams are generated; general municipal solid waste handling is the only applicable disposal standard, with no industrial discharge or environmental emission limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and occupational workplace clearance are required for the leased office premises; structural load inspections do not apply to non-industrial office use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Treasury, and Customs of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (Revenue Division); corporate registry administered by the Office of the Associate Registrar of Corporations (Marshall Islands Corporate Registry). No national tax filing portal exists because the RMI levies no income tax, VAT, payroll tax, or capital tax on non-resident domestic corporations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity obtains its sole statutory identifier by incorporating a Business Corporation (BC) under the Business Corporations Act and registering as a non-resident domestic corporation under the Non-Resident Domestic Corporations Act 2001 (NRDCA). No separate TIN or VAT ID is issued; the Registrar's certificate registration number is the sole fiscal identifier for banking, KYC, Stripe/Paddle onboarding, and all compliance purposes. No annual tax return, tax election filing, or iterative tax-ID procurement procedure applies to a tax-exempt non-resident BC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — a non-resident domestic BC is categorically exempt from Marshall Islands income tax, withholding tax, capital gains tax, and all indirect taxes; taxation is neither pass-through nor entity-level for RMI purposes, as the BC's non-resident status is the exclusive determinant of tax immunity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election and no hybrid-mismatch election exists under RMI law. The operative statutory election is designation of the BC as a non-resident domestic corporation (tax-exempt) versus a resident domestic corporation (technically taxable at nominal rates); foreign owners of remote software and IoT telemetry businesses must file and maintain non-resident status. No elective VAT or GST registration is available because no VAT/GST regime exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT, GST, or sales-and-use tax in force. The only indirect-type levies are import customs and excise duties on physical goods, which never attach to remote screen-share or IoT telematic services delivered electronically.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — the Marshall Islands imposes no indirect-tax registration threshold; economic turnover concepts are inoperative for digital services, and a non-resident BC owes no VAT/GST registration or collection obligation regardless of global revenue.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None — there is no e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API transmission, or digital stamping mandate in the RMI. A BC may issue paper or PDF invoices in any commercial format without tax-authority pre-approval; invoicing for remote desktop access and unattended-machine telemetry subscriptions is governed solely by contract law and by the customer's destination jurisdiction (e.g., EU digital-services VAT, US sales tax, or digital-services withholding in the customer's country).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable — with no VAT/GST in the Marshall Islands, no zero-rating claim or export VAT refund is required or available for remote screen-share software, telemetry, or IoT services. Income from such offshore digital services is exempt from RMI taxation by operation of the NRDCA, and a foreign-owned non-resident BC cannot incur RMI indirect tax on export receipts. No filing, ruling, or statutory application is required to invoke the exemption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — not applicable: RMI Customs does not process or require an export declaration for intangible software or telemetry services delivered electronically.
Bill of Lading — not applicable: no physical movement of goods occurs in remote desktop access services, and no shipping document can or should be generated.
Inward Remittance Certificate — not required: the RMI has no foreign-exchange controls and does not mandate repatriation certificates or central-bank approval for USD software subscription receipts.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT zero-rating clawback can arise because no VAT is imposed in the RMI. The operative risks are status-based: filing a false non-resident declaration, abusing the non-resident election while deriving RMI-source income, or failing to maintain registered-agent and corporate records. Consequences include registry de-registration and strike-off, monetary penalties under the NRDCA, reinstatement costs, and director or agent liability. The 180-day figure in this dossier is a standardized pipeline placeholder carrying no RMI statutory force; US-source digital receipts remain independently subject to IRS enforcement and applicable US state sales-tax regimes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commission of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (Superintendent of Banking); no domestic central bank exists, and the U.S. dollar is official legal tender under the RMI–U.S. Compact of Free Association.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The U.S. dollar is fully convertible across both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange controls, surrender requirements, or central bank approvals. Dividend remittances, capital injections, and profit repatriation are unrestricted for non-resident-owned Business Corporations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies. Export receipts in U.S. dollars may be freely retained, credited to offshore accounts, or disbursed without reference to any central bank conversion requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam (Republic of the Marshall Islands Branch)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-Low. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., U.K. or E.U. e-money institutions) can provide rapid multi-currency collection points for software subscription revenue, but they do not constitute licensed banks in the Marshall Islands, offer no local guarantee of clearing finality, and are generally unable to support statutory capital escrow structures. Use is legally permissible when supported by contractual disclosure and full AML/KYC documentation, but a domestic or high-grade offshore banking relationship remains mandatory for robust liquidity and inbound wire verification.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: RMI regulations do not mandate physical director attendance, but correspondent banking pressure means domestic banks generally require either an in-person interview of the ultimate beneficial owner or a formally supervised remote video interview combined with notarized corporate documents, apostilled passports, proof of address, and bank reference checks. Fully remote onboarding is available on a case-by-case basis under enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital injection or inadequate discernible economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn source-of-funds statement; audited financial statements or CPA-certified management accounts; corporate registry certificate and certificate of good standing; substance-relevant business plan evidencing remote software licensing, third-party server contracts, product usage, and projected revenue through Stripe and Paddle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident Board of Directors without physical local presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of passports, proof of residential address, professional references from regulated financial institutions, video-verification completion report, and apostilled power of attorney enabling the RMI registered agent to accept service of process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP exposure, or opaque beneficial-ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed ownership chart up to ultimate beneficial owners, sanctions and PEP screening from a reputable compliance vendor, negative-media search results, sworn non-affiliation declaration, and legal opinion from an RMI-licensed counsel confirming absence of OFAC, E.U., U.N., and U.K. sanctions nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank's due-diligence concern over IT services and software licensing payment flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete platform documentation and customer contracts for remote screen-share and unattended IoT telemetry software; data-processing and privacy policy; sub-processor agreements; historical transaction reports from Stripe and Paddle demonstrating genuine recurring subscription revenues; and reasoned explanation of remote-support commercial model.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound non-resident capital contributions should be routed as U.S.-dollar SWIFT MT103 credits to the RMI beneficiary bank or to a named U.S.-dollar clearing account held by the entity. Remittance purpose must state 'Capital contribution for software development and working capital—non-resident Business Corporation; no exchange-control approval required.' The sending institution must provide full beneficiary name, account number, and address, together with source-of-funds supporting documentation; the receiving RMI bank will conduct OFAC, sanctions, and internal large-credit verification before crediting the account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements should settle through SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers, Fedwire/CHIPS for domestic U.S.-dollar clearing, or a Commercial Letter of Credit issued by the RMI relationship bank and confirmed by a reputable U.S. or E.U. bank for procurement of hardware or dedicated servers. Operational vendor payments for software licensing and cloud infrastructure should use standard MT103 rails with references to the underlying invoice and service contract.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards on G10 currencies
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for hedges involving non-convertible or restricted currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually due by 30 September; first report due by 30 September following incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: USD 100 late penalty for filing after 30 September; failure to file for two consecutive years may result in administrative dissolution by the Registrar.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit threshold for non-public Marshall Islands Business Corporations; audits are voluntary unless required by listing, creditors, shareholders, or external verification.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No local GAAP mandates; IFRS or US GAAP commonly applied; Business Corporation Act requires books and records reflecting true financial condition.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation filing required under Marshall Islands law; register of members must be kept current with share transfers, and no statutory obligation exists to file shareholding confirmations with the Registrar.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; voluntary audit USD 3,000 - 8,000 if engaged

approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
